subsystems.name: Silicon neurons
subsystems.role: generate electrical spikes when their internal state crosses a threshold, mimicking biological neurons.

subsystems.name: Synapse array
subsystems.role: stores the connection strengths (weights) and applies them to incoming spikes.

subsystems.name: Spike routing network
subsystems.role: delivers each spike only to the neurons it connects to, without a global clock.

subsystems.name: Learning engine
subsystems.role: updates weights locally using rules such as spike-timing-dependent plasticity.

subsystems.name: I/O and sensor interface
subsystems.role: connects to event-based sensors and host systems.

subsystems.name: Power and clock management
subsystems.role: keeps energy per spike extremely low, often by avoiding a global clock.

buildSteps.title: Design neuron and synapse circuits
buildSteps.detail: Engineers choose analog or digital designs and simulate them to ensure reliable spiking at low energy.

buildSteps.title: Lay out the chip
buildSteps.detail: Custom analog blocks and digital routers are placed and routed, often mixing custom and synthesized logic.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate at a foundry
buildSteps.detail: The design is taped out on a CMOS process, sometimes with embedded non-volatile memory for weights.

buildSteps.title: Test and characterise
buildSteps.detail: Wafer probing measures spike timing, energy per spike and variability across the chip.

buildSteps.title: Package and integrate
buildSteps.detail: The die is packaged and connected to event-based sensors, memory and host interfaces.

buildSteps.title: Build the software stack
buildSteps.detail: Compilers map trained SNNs onto the hardware, and frameworks run the network and monitor learning.

buildSteps.title: Deploy at the edge
buildSteps.detail: The chip runs always-on tasks such as keyword spotting or gesture recognition in battery-powered devices.

prerequisites.why: cameras and microphones that output spikes natively feed neuromorphic chips efficiently, but they are not yet mainstream.
training SNNs with backpropagation is difficult; most methods are still research-grade.
analog weights need dense, low-energy storage, and resistive RAM or flash are not yet ideal.
neuromorphic chips are built on standard silicon processes, so this is available.
compilers and frameworks exist but are immature and fragmented, slowing adoption.

pathway.milestone: commercial and research chips for niche always-on sensing
pathway.unlocks: ultra-low-power keyword spotting and gesture recognition in small devices.

pathway.milestone: standardised toolchains and larger SNN models
pathway.unlocks: easier integration into mainstream AI pipelines and hybrid systems.

pathway.milestone: tight integration with event-based sensors for autonomous systems
pathway.unlocks: low-latency, low-power perception for robots and wearables.

pathway.milestone: on-chip learning and adaptation at scale
pathway.unlocks: edge devices that learn continuously without cloud connection.
